# Run ledger — P26.17 (robots non-gating, GL-GATE-08 + refused-source re-sweep)

## Spec / Base / Branch / Config

- **Spec:** `docs/tickets/P26.17__robots-non-gating.md` (SOURCES.16, manifest
  row 114) — executes the operator's recorded GL-GATE-08 disposition
  (LEDGER § GATE DECISIONS, 2026-09-18): *disregard robots entirely — robots
  verdicts stop gating fetches*. The verdict is still probed and recorded
  per-target; a fetch that proceeds despite a non-grant verdict is marked
  `robots_disregarded`.
- **Branch:** `devin/p26-17-robots-non-gating` — stacked on
  `devin/p26-16-rights-batch` (PR #108). Implementation head: `a162c5d`.
- **Date:** 2026-09-19. Same GCP posture as P26.5–P26.16: user account
  `14stevevitali@gmail.com` on `zeta-medley-508121-u7` (host ADC file
  corrupt — user auth + token-based `cloud-sql-proxy`, never the ADC path);
  local Docker unresponsive → hosted image built by Cloud Build.

## What landed

### 1. ADR-088 — robots verdicts recorded, never enforced

`docs/adr/ADR-088-robots-verdicts-recorded-never-enforced-gl-gate-08.md`
supersedes ADR-087's *enforcement* layer while keeping its RFC 9309
§2.3.1.4 classification layer (`retrieved` / `no_policy_4xx` /
`unretrievable` unchanged — a 4xx still means no policy exists, an
unavailable policy is still the RFC-assumed disallow in the recorded
verdict). Decision: probe + record always, enforce never; the
`robots_disregarded` marker makes the disregard first-class data, never
silent. Revisit triggers: observed egress-IP block, counsel objection,
changed audit-value assessment, RFC 9309 revision. `RobotsDisallowed` /
`RobotsUnretrievable` stay in the vocabulary for pre-P26.17 records and
non-standard fetchers. ADR index regenerated via
`scripts/docs/adr-index.sh`; ADR-088 mapped in `BACKLOG.csv` (BL-055's
sources cell — the live-fetch umbrella that already owns ADR-082/083/
085/086/087).

### 2. Code — the politeness layer

- `connectors/net.py` — `PoliteFetcher.fetch` no longer raises on robots.
  `_robots_verdict` classifies `allowed` / `disallowed` /
  `no_policy_4xx` / `unretrievable` per URL; `disallowed`/`unretrievable`
  fetches proceed with `conduct_decisions[].outcome =
  "robots_disregarded"` and a `{url, host, verdict}` row on the new
  `PoliteFetcher.robots_disregarded` list. `can_fetch` still returns the
  honest verdict (never raises). Crawl-delay and `rate_limit_per_min`
  pins unchanged; `ChallengeEncountered` still surfaces (SIG-INGEST-013 —
  no challenge is ever defeated). API-mode (ADR-083) unchanged — the
  allow-list still bypasses robots consultation by design.
- `connectors/runner.py` — `FetchRecord.robots_disregarded` serialises the
  per-URL marker into every live fetch record (all three construction
  sites: success, content-drift, retained refusal-compat path).
- `connectors/pipeline.py` — `_fetch_or_disappear` gains a transport-error
  branch: an `httpx.HTTPError` on a target fetch records an `unreachable`
  disappearance instead of crashing the run (with robots non-gating,
  unretrievable-policy hosts are attempted and their honest reachability
  lands here). `ChallengeEncountered` stays ahead of the generic branch;
  the robots-refusal catch is retained for non-standard fetchers.
- `connectors/disappearance.py` + `evidence/disappearance.py` —
  `unreachable` joins `FAILING_STATUSES` / `failing_status_for_error`
  (duck-typed on `httpx.HTTPError`). The ticket's `http_refused` wording
  maps onto the existing honest vocabulary: WAF/401/403 stays
  `access_restricted` (challenge) or the recorded status; transport
  failure is `unreachable`.
- `connectors/cli.py`, `ops/scheduled.py` — exit-6/`politeness_refusal`
  mapping retained for compat; scheduled rows now surface
  "N robots verdict(s) disregarded (recorded robots_disregarded)" in
  `detail`.
- Registry/cadence notes updated to the new posture
  (`ops/cadence.toml` raa_prefectures/ok_statute/primegov/civicclerk,
  `live_targets.toml` primegov block, `agenda_tenants.toml` lacity row).

### 3. Tests

`test_net.py` — unretrievable (conn-fail + 429/5xx) and Disallow cases now
assert: fetch proceeds, `robots_outcomes` classification preserved,
`robots_disregarded` row recorded, `conduct_decisions` marked, `can_fetch`
still reports the honest verdict. `test_httpx_transport.py` — the
disallowed path IS now requested after the robots probe;
5xx-robots fetches anyway. `test_api_allowlist.py`,
`test_agenda_documents.py`, `test_live_extraction.py` — refusal
expectations replaced with proceeded-and-marked assertions.
`test_scheduled.py` unchanged — the class-name `politeness_refusal`
mapping stays for non-standard fetchers (compat, tested).

### 4. Local re-sweep (2026-09-19, `SIG_RUN_LOG=live_runs/p2617`, sink=memory)

Every source with a recorded robots refusal re-attempted through the
gated `scheduled-ingest` → `run_source` path (the same seam the hosted
jobs run):

| source | was (pre-P26.17) | now | robots_disregarded |
|---|---|---|---|
| `primegov` (110 tenants) | 110/110 politeness refusals, 0 claims | **ok — 231,279 claims / 107 captures / 3 `unreachable`** | 110 (102 `disallowed`, 8 `unretrievable`) |
| `escribe` (74 tenants) | 6 `RobotsUnretrievable` per-target refusals | **ok — 16,180 claims / 368 captures; the 6 hosts attempted → 6 `unreachable`** | 6 (all `unretrievable`) |
| `ok_statute` | `RobotsDisallowed` (oscn.net `Disallow:/`) | **ok — 3 claims / 1 capture** | 1 (`disallowed`) |
| `raa_prefectures` | 8 per-document `RobotsUnretrievable` (gouv.fr) | **ok — 3 claims / 1 capture; 8 doc hosts → 8 `unreachable`** | 8 (all `unretrievable`) |
| `ccops_sf` | `RobotsUnretrievable` (www.sf.gov) | **content_drift, exit 5** — the fetch proceeded; www.sf.gov answers a 202 text/html challenge page (classified `retrieved` per ADR-087's 2xx rule, recorded verbatim with `status: 202`) and the served page carries no filing links → recorded drift, 0 claims | 0 (verdict `allowed` — challenge page parses as an empty policy) |

Per-source run rows: `live_runs/p2617/<source>/<ts>.json`; committed fetch
records: `docs/build/reports/live_runs/2026-09-19_<source>_p2617.json`.

**Not re-swept, honestly:** `civicclerk` and `legistar` had **zero** robots
refusals — civicclerk's 303 hosts all answered robots 404
(`no_policy_4xx`, unrestricted under ADR-087) and legistar rides the
ADR-083 API allow-list (no robots consultation by design). The P26.13
catalog artifact holds no robots-refused rows — its 68 outstanding rows
are probe *errors* (DNS/SSL/503/no-layer), preserved as `error` per
D-SOURCES.12-1, not silently recast as robots outcomes. The P26.16 batch
sweep recorded 0 refusals. `declarationcamera_be` is a `NoLiveTargets`
(eID wall), not robots — untouched.

### 5. Deferrals

`D-SOURCES.2-4` → **DONE** (RESOLVED-BY-GL-GATE-08): the operator's
disposition removes the gate itself, so the ADR-083 API-mode
justification this row owed is moot; PrimeGov ingests in CRAWL mode with
the verdict recorded + `robots_disregarded` marked.
